# Design

Three waves with one shape each. Wave 1 is repair plus scaffolding: seven tasks that each own one red continuous-integration job or job pair and fix what it names, and six tasks that build the explorer's own gates - the containerised mix runner every later Elixir task qualifies through, one lint script per language, the test-ratio script, the two CI jobs and the two bounded fleet gates. Wave 2 is the fork's remaining surface, twelve tasks whose touched paths are disjoint so they run in parallel: the frontend theme owns the toolkit theme, the presets and the marks; search owns the search bar and its routing helper; the receipt detail page owns its route, its view and its types; the API schema task owns the Paxeer X controllers and the schema modules; the event-decoding pair owns first the new tables and their runners and then the transform; the isolation task owns the factory and the fetcher it defeats; and the copy tool, the deployment definitions, the boot fix, the wrapped-coin contract and the retirement of the duplicate explorer surface each own their own tree. Wave 3 runs the aggregate explorer suites once on the merged revision and writes the gate records.
